minutes.headline: Stormwater Task Force named a vice chair and reviewed a draft outreach presentation for a proposed stormwater utility.
minutes.summary: The task force held a short vote to appoint a vice chair, then spent most of the meeting going through a draft public-outreach PowerPoint for a proposed stormwater utility (Enterprise fund). They discussed a possible resident fee, commercial charges, and which town boards to brief and when. March minutes were approved with a minor spelling correction and the meeting adjourned.

budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW drainage line has been flat and he asked for an increase for the coming year; the recommended budget has already gone out.
The storm response was estimated to have cost the town a notable amount, which would fall under a rainy-day emergency response category in the proposed utility.
A fee on the order of $100 per year per resident across about 4,000 properties was discussed, billed quarterly.

Commercial properties were proposed to cover a significant part of a roughly million-dollar target, with a shortfall noted; whether a million is too high or covers startup versus yearly costs was unsettled.
First-year cost was discussed as higher because of equipment purchases, with a lower ongoing amount afterward; spreading equipment costs by loan was mentioned.
Members considered the per-resident charge and treated about 100 dollars a year as the ceiling, with a lower residential rate desirable.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town-owned properties may be exempt, and the group discussed that the regular budget stormwater line would transfer into the Enterprise fund.

John will continue fine-tuning the outreach presentation and send it to everyone for comments.
Briefings of the Select Board are to wait until after the election, likely the first June meeting; Nick to be asked to review slides and possibly present.
Next meeting set for the third Thursday, the 16th.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force appointed a vice chair by voice vote; the count was not audible in the recording.
Most of the meeting went to a draft public-outreach presentation for a proposed stormwater utility run as an Enterprise fund, including a possible resident fee and commercial charges.
Members agreed to keep money and fee figures out of public discussion until after the election.
Briefings of the Select Board were set to wait until after the election, likely the first June meeting; Bill is to approach the Planning Board about enforcement and bylaws.
March minutes were approved with a spelling correction, and the next meeting was set for the third Thursday, the 16th.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility would move drainage costs from the general budget into a separate fee-funded Enterprise fund, which could appear as a new charge on property owners' bills.
The fee level, the commercial share and the startup-versus-ongoing cost were still unsettled in this meeting, so residents have not yet been shown a number they could be asked to vote on.
watch_next: The next task force meeting on the third Thursday, the 16th.
Select Board briefing on the utility, expected around the first June meeting, after the election.
